title: Elice Shares Top IPO Price After Worst Major Korea Debut
summary:
The AI infrastructure company has regained its footing in Seoul, climbing for two consecutive sessions since a sharp selloff on Oct. 20. Shares of neocloud provider Elice now trade above their initial public offering price, reversing a brutal trading debut on the Kosdaq market where the stock plummeted 32%. Market participants previously described the slide as the worst opening-day performance for a major IPO in South Korean history.

Elice raised $151 million at a $750 million valuation in an offering that was oversubscribed by 400 times. While the initial crash weighed on the KOSPI index and sparked volatility in other global data center stocks, strong earnings from US tech firms have since lifted sentiment. The company is on track to at least double its revenue this year, CEO Jaewon stated, as the firm expands its GPU cloud rental and operations services.

selectedTweets.text:
According to Korean media, Elice Group just hit the daily LIMIT UP on its second day of trading.

The Korean AI cloud company fell 31.93% on its KOSDAQ debut yesterday, closing at 61,600 won against an IPO price of 90,500 won.

But this morning it jumped 29.92% to 79,900 won, but it is still trading below where it priced.

Bloomberg and Reuters treated the first day crash as a sign that investors are losing faith in neoclouds, and CNBC said the selloff spilled into data center stocks in the United States like $CRWV and $NBIS.

The IPO raised only about $150 million, but the market treated it as a referendum on the entire AI infrastructure trade.

One day later, buyers stepped right back in and sentiment on AI infrastructure is swinging HARD but the demand for compute has not changed.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
$SPY rose about 0.2% today to around $768, bouncing from an early low of $764.25 as the Dow led and tech lagged.

Here are the top stories you need to know.

1. South Korean neocloud Elice plunged 32% in its trading debut, dragging the KOSPI down about 4% and reviving fears of AI compute overcapacity.

2. Chip stocks shook off that early selloff and turned green, with $AMD, $TSM, $MRVL and $MU all trading higher while $NVDA finished near flat.

3. $CRWV jumped about 4% as it tried to bounce from last week's debt driven selloff, one day after Goldman Sachs upgraded it to Buy.

4. The Dow jumped about 500 points as Brent crude slipped below $110 on reports of progress in United States and Iran diplomacy.

5. Investors rotated out of tech and into healthcare and value stocks, with $LLY up almost 4% and the Russell 2000 up about 1.7%.

6. $META fell more than 2% and $GOOGL fell more than 1% ahead of big tech earnings, with $META and $TSLA reporting tomorrow after the close.

7. Reuters reports OpenAI is racing to raise about $30 billion at a valuation above $1.4 trillion before Anthropic's expected IPO in mid November.

8. $MMM rose about 6% after expanding its data center partnership with $AMZN and giving Amazon warrants to buy more than $521 million of its stock.

9. The United States 10 year Treasury yield fell to about 5.10% after weak housing data, and the odds of a Fed rate hike next week dropped to about 15%.

10. $SPCX and $NFLX report earnings after the close today, with investors watching SpaceX for clues on its AI spending plans.
